title: SAES search log
description: Records a single literature search run during the SETUP stage. One file per search. Committed to version control alongside the question framing document and screening decisions.

search_id.description: Short slug identifying this search, e.g. 'asgm-biodiversity-2026-05'. Used to cross-reference from screening_decisions.csv and downstream provenance.

research_question_ref.description: Path to the framing document that this search is operationalising. Usually 'question_framing.md'.

database.description: Source database. OpenAlex is the default; other supported values are 'Scopus', 'Web of Science', 'PubMed', 'Google Scholar', 'snowball-from-seed'.

search_url.description: The full URL as submitted to the database, including all filter parameters. For snowball searches, the URL of the seed paper.

search_string_human_readable.description: The boolean search string in a form a human reader can interpret without parsing the URL. Should match the meaning of search_url.

filters_applied.description: One entry per filter beyond the core search string. Each filter must carry a rationale linking it to the framing document.

filter.description: The filter as expressed in the API, e.g. 'from_publication_date:2000-01-01'.

rationale.description: Why this filter was applied. Usually a reference to a scope boundary in the framing document.

run_date.description: ISO-8601 date when the search was executed. OpenAlex content changes over time, so this matters for reproducibility.

result_count.description: Total result count returned by the database (e.g. OpenAlex meta.count). Note discrepancies between this and the screened count in screening_decisions.csv in 'notes' if any.

snapshot_id.description: Optional. The OpenAlex snapshot release identifier, if the user is pinning to a specific snapshot rather than the live API. Recommended for high-stakes syntheses.

protocol_version.description: SAES protocol version under which this search was conducted, e.g. 'v0.2.0-alpha'.

notes.description: Free text. Anything a future reader needs to know — e.g. 'first run returned 2; re-ran without is_oa filter; new count 87' or 'large language model used to suggest synonym expansion, see chat log on date X'.
